answer: I ran the 3-qubit GHZ circuit on sirius:mock with 200 shots. The circuit was H on qubit 0, CNOT 0 to 1, CNOT 1 to 2, and a measurement of all 3 qubits. I submitted one job, 01a15f17-b288-7371-b4b2-a2a792718bce, and it finished with counts {"000": 200}. A real GHZ state would split the shots about evenly between 000 and 111. All 200 shots came back 000, which is a sign that the mock backend returns placeholder results and does not simulate the circuit. These counts confirm that the job submission works end to end. They do not show any real quantum behavior. The script is at /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_1a6926f8-f6c-46/scratch/ghz.py.
